answer: Because the forge salt is published after the sable checkpoint, the pulse audit recomputes each digest and a prepared batch fails verification. An operator running 52 keys thus burns for 52 live submissions inside the window instead of preparing them in bulk, which removes the advantage of scale. Answers are salted with a 130 bit value revealed only at epoch close, so a text prepared before the reveal cannot be pre-hashed against it. That is 21 dollars per alias. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
